title: Report per-rule reading refusal counts in status; flag rules over 30%
summary: Add to `athena status` a per-reading-rule count of first readings refused and second readings still refused over the last 50 readings. Make the Hestia sweep flag any rule refusing more than 30% of first readings, naming the rule and its most common refusal text. Goal: measure which reading rules cause re-reads, so the reader brief or the rule can be fixed. Audience: the owner and the Hestia sweep.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria require new tests plus fmt, clippy -D warnings and cargo test.
Criteria run tests on fixture reading records and check the reported counts and flags.
An empty or tiny window gives no flag and is not reported as healthy.
The CHANGELOG entry and code docs are written for an outside reader.
The change measures rule refusals by rule rather than counting retries only.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: I read crates/athena-core/src/status.rs (StatusView, `status` at line 985), crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs (`default_checks`, `run_sweep`, `repeated_causes`), crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs (rule functions named check_*, `ReadingCheck::Accept` and `Refuse(String)`) and crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs (the refused-then-reread test at line 1855). Resolution order: the reader runs, rules run in turn, and the first refusal triggers one re-read whose brief carries the refusal text. A second refusal is the failure, and the reader does not run a third time. Reader invocations are recorded under `<job>/invocations/`. I found no stored refusal text or rule name per reading, so the producer must first find where the first refusal's text can be read back from records and add the smallest record field if there is none. A new record or field under crates/ must be covered by `check_record_file`, `AnyRecord` and the round-trip test. The property is measured directly from per-reading refusal data, not from a stand-in such as invocation counts alone.

Rule identification: a refusal text is mapped to a rule by the check function name (for example `check_governance_coverage`) or by a stable text prefix. Text that matches no rule is counted under 'other'.

Window: the last 50 readings means the 50 most recent jobs that have a reading, counted per job. A first refusal counts once per rule that refused it. A second refusal counts the rules that refused the re-read. The sweep rate is first refusals by that rule divided by first readings in the window.

Fewer than a minimum number of readings in the window, for example 10, does not trigger a flag, so an empty or tiny window is never reported as healthy or as a failure. This is a design choice the producer states in docs or tests.

Existing deliverables beyond the three named files (reading.rs, run/mod.rs, athena-data records.rs, a docs page) are possible only if the refusal data is not already recorded; they are listed with lower probability.

The change adds no refusal rule. It only measures refusals, so no 'higher refusal rate is intended' or replay percentage criterion is needed. Governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml and others) are untouched. Prompts are untouched; the reader prompt has 2 tokens of headroom.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-core status`. A test in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs builds fixture reading records where rule A refuses 3 first readings and 1 second reading, and rule B refuses 1 first reading. It asserts that the status output reports, per rule, the first-refusal count and the second-refusal count, over at most the last 50 readings.
Run `cargo test -p athena-core status`. A test with fixture records of more than 50 readings asserts that only the most recent 50 are counted.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core hestia`. A test in crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs asserts that the sweep flags a rule refusing more than 30% of first readings. The flag names the rule and its most common refusal text. The same test asserts that a rule at or under 30% is not flagged.
Run `cargo test -p athena-core hestia`. A test asserts that a window with no readings, or fewer than the stated minimum, produces no flag and no claim that the rules are healthy.
Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test`. All pass.
CHANGELOG.md has a new entry. It names the per-rule first and second refusal counts in `athena status` and the Hestia sweep flag above 30%.

The diff in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs shows each reading rule listed with its two counts. The diff in crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs shows the 30% threshold as a named constant, not a bare number.
If the diff adds a record type or field under crates/, it is covered by `check_record_file`, `AnyRecord` parsing and the round-trip test. Run `cargo test -p athena-data` to confirm.

out_of_scope: Changing, adding or loosening any reading rule or its refusal text
Editing the reader prompt or brief; the sweep only names which rule or brief to fix
Automatically filing fix requests for flagged rules
Changing the retry limit of one re-read
departures: The cost, time and acceptance figures are worse than the reference. The refusal text and rule name per reading do not appear to be recorded, so the producer may need to add a record field and touch more crates. Rule-name mapping and the Hestia check add judgment, and the reading rules in this area refuse often.
urgent_reason: It measures how many reader calls and retries each reading rule causes, which is the wasted time the request describes.
hard_reason: Adds a Hestia sweep check that flags rules which refuse work, and changes how reading refusals are measured in the run pipeline.
